title: Python Classes and Objects
learningObjectives: Explain the core concepts of Python Classes and Objects.
Choose an appropriate object-oriented design for a small Python problem.
Trace object state and method calls accurately.
Apply Python class features with correct method and attribute behavior.
Recognize design trade-offs, edge cases and maintainability concerns.

understand.concept: A class statement creates a class object and its indented suite defines attributes and methods. Calling the class constructs an instance. Attributes can be read through dot notation; methods are functions defined in the class and normally receive the instance as their first parameter.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding class construction and instance access is the foundation for reading and designing Python object models.
understand.analogy: A class is a blueprint; an instance is one built object. The blueprint describes possible features, while each built object carries its own values.
understand.summary: Python Classes and Objects introduces a focused part of Python's object model and its practical use.

explain.narrative: Study the concept, trace the receiver and state for each operation, then run the examples. Pay attention to Python's conventions and documented protocol behavior rather than assuming that class syntax provides strict access control.

examples.title: Create and instantiate
examples.code:
class Animal:
    pass
dog = Animal()
print(isinstance(dog, Animal))
examples.explanation: isinstance checks whether an object belongs to a class or its subclasses.

examples.title: Define a class attribute
examples.code:
class Device:
    category = 'electronics'
phone = Device()
print(phone.category)
examples.explanation: A class attribute is shared through the class unless shadowed on an instance.

examples.title: Define an instance method
examples.explanation: Calling a bound method supplies its instance automatically.

examples.title: Check class membership
examples.code:
class Vehicle: pass
class Car(Vehicle): pass
car = Car()
print(isinstance(car, Vehicle))
examples.explanation: Instances of a subclass also satisfy isinstance for the base class.

examples.title: Use class identity
examples.code:
class Token: pass
first = Token()
second = Token()
print(first is second)
examples.explanation: Two separately constructed objects have distinct identities.

practise.guidedTask: Build a small program that demonstrates python classes and objects. Write down the object types, relevant attributes, method calls and expected state changes before running it.
practise.independentTask: Extend the example into a small domain model of your choice. Add validation, clear method names, boundary tests and a short explanation of why your design uses classes rather than simpler functions or data structures.
hints: Identify which object owns each piece of state.
Trace the first argument supplied to every bound method.
Prefer explicit invariants and small public interfaces.
Test at least one boundary or unsupported input.
Use composition when it models the relationship more accurately than inheritance.
practise.challenge: Refactor the model into a testable design with clear responsibilities, documented public behavior and tests for normal, boundary and invalid cases.
validationCriteria: All five examples execute on the supported Python version and match their outputs.
The implementation follows Python's documented class and special-method semantics.
State changes are scoped to the intended object or class.
Unsupported inputs produce a deliberate result or a clear exception.
The design avoids unnecessary inheritance, shared mutable defaults and misleading private-access claims.
